metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets The Dominican Republic

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 results for the Dominican Republic using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The document describes international comparisons and uncertainty intervals (95% confidence intervals) and notes that some countries/economies did not meet PISA sampling standards (asterisks), implying that PISA’s complex sampling design and associated estimation procedures are used in the underlying database. However, the factsheet does not specify the exact student weight variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were applied. Because this is a descriptive reporting factsheet rather than an ML modeling paper, the manuscript does not provide a data-preparation pipeline (e.g., filtering rules or weight application details) beyond the PISA technical standards caveats.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive OECD factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking performance and related associations (e.g., differences by gender and socio-economic quartiles). It does not present an analysis pipeline that explicitly reports how plausible values (PVs) for creative thinking were handled, nor does it describe a missing-data strategy for an empirical model. As a result, PV and missing-data handling details are not available in the provided text, representing a reporting gap for methodological transparency.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports the Dominican Republic results for PISA 2022 creative thinking, stating that 6,868 students in 253 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 121,900 15-year-olds (an estimated 64% of the total population of 15-year-olds). No additional inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., specific creative-thinking module completion thresholds, missing-data exclusions, or grade restrictions) are described in the provided text; therefore, the analytic sample is taken as the PISA 2022 national sample used for the reported creative thinking estimates.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD factsheet summarizes PISA 2022 Creative Thinking results for 15-year-old students in the Dominican Republic. It reports overall creative thinking proficiency on a 60-point scale, with a mean score of 15, significantly below the OECD average (33). It also provides proficiency-level distributions (19% at Level 3+; 1% at Level 5–6) and relative performance patterns across ideation processes (generating diverse ideas vs generating creative ideas vs evaluating and improving ideas) and domain contexts (written, visual, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). The factsheet further describes within-country gaps by socio-economic quartiles (advantaged students +5.7 points) and gender (+2.6 points for girls), and highlights associations between creative thinking and students’ beliefs/attitudes (e.g., fixed mindset linked to lower scores). Methodological details on PV handling, missing data, and weighting variables are not specified in the provided text, and some international comparisons require caution due to PISA sampling-standard caveats.
